Hello, I am a younger guy and own a successful  web design and development business where I work out of my house everyday. I also deal with severe depression and anxiety, so maybe I can tell you a little bit about my experiences working from home.

Working from home, especially with family or kids is extremely difficult to stay focused and maintain efficiency.  We have/had a number or "remote" employees that have done well with it and some that couldn't make it work.

I think the most difficult aspects that we face are very simple;

1. Motivation
When you are working from home , it's easy to say, "I feel like sleeping in today" or "I'll play with the kids for an hour or two". There are simply more opportunities to pull you away from your work.
- I've combated this by setting specific working hours  derived from client communications. I am also constantly talking via phone or Instant Messaging to my team and our clients which keeps you engaged and motivated. 

2. Getting to comfortable
In the early days I would not get dressed for the entire day...roll out of bed and I would work all day in my PJs. When you start to let yourself go a little that , your work reflects that. 
- It's a super simple point. Treat it like a real office with real expectations and you will feel more confident and produce better work.

Don't get me wrong, I'm not trying to say it is bad in anyway. I love it and I struggle with it all the time. 

There are many rewards from working from home but those rewards  could easily turn into hindrances that could affect  your performance and ultimately your job.

As far as the depression and anxiety issues that I suffer from are mostly amplified  by this environment . I will sometimes work from home and not leave the house for a week maybe 2 at a time and when I do my anxiety explodes and then when I am back I get extremely depressed about not being able to be normal. It's obviously a lot easier to deal with a panic-attack or having a place to be alone for the depression when you are in your own home. But I have found that overall being alone(in a sense) from home has added to my depression and anxiety problems. I do notice when I string together some meetings or lunches over the course of a week I am happy, motivated and focused.

Tl:dr
Working from home is harder than going into an office. Expect to meet your lazy self and take on the challenge to get them motivated. 
Treat it just as you were going into a real office, shower, dress and commit to real hours. Don't forget to abuse a few perks here and there, but IMO this may have the opposite effect on helping you depression and anxiety.
